rows.uncertainty: Abstract only. It gives no patient, lesion or graft counts and does not separate IGH results from vitiligo and postinflammatory leukoderma. 'Melanocytes were present in the successful grafts' implies some grafts were not successful; the number or share of failed grafts is not in abstract. 'Successful' repigmentation is not defined. The only timing given is repigmentation visible within 7 to 14 days; follow-up length after grafting is not in abstract, so months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE from this source (full text needed). Full text is subscription only (Europe PMC: not in PMC, Subscription required).
rows.citation: Suvanprakorn P, Dee-Ananlap S, Pongsomboon C, Klaus SN. J Am Acad Dermatol 1985;13(6):968-974

quotes.quote: Patients with three types of leukoderma--vitiligo, idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis, and postinflammatory leukoderma--had successful repigmentation after transplantation of autologous melanocytes.
Blisters were produced by suction or by freezing with liquid nitrogen. The roof of the blister from donor skin was grafted to the raw surface of the recipient site.
Repigmentation was visible within 7 to 14 days.
Histochemical studies confirmed the absence of dopa-positive cells in the areas of leukoderma prior to grafting. Melanocytes were present in the successful grafts.
Melanocytes were present in the successful grafts.
